description.value: Compact BC Parks campground in a scenic canyon on Highway 20, set beside the glacier-blue Chilcotin River with a short interpretive trail and nearby fishing and wildlife watching; the river is cold and fast-moving (no swimming), and gates are locked from mid-September to mid-May.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website for Bull Canyon Park provided rich, direct evidence. Key cycling-relevant facts: the site is explicitly identified as the only provincial campsite along Highway 20 between Williams Lake and Tweedsmuir Park, making it strategically vital for touring cyclists; a dedicated cycling section explicitly addresses e-bikes (restricted to roads, not trails); the park page prominently features a 'Book camping' call-to-action linked to frontcountry camping reservations, confirming reservations are accepted. Most granular amenity details (water, showers, food storage, etc.) were not mentioned in the fetched content, so those remain null per the rules.
concerns: No phone number or street address present in OSM record.
Campground gates are locked off-season (September 16 to May 14); cycle tourists must confirm the site is open before planning around it.
E-bikes are explicitly restricted to park roads and not permitted on the Chilcotin River Interpretive Trail, per the website cycling section.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Bull Canyon is a legitimate, active BC Parks frontcountry campground and the only provincial campsite along the Highway 20 Chilcotin corridor between Williams Lake and Tweedsmuir Park — a strategically indispensable overnight stop for touring cyclists on one of BC's most remote paved routes.
enrichment_extras.notes: Nearest community is Alexis Creek, approximately 6 km east on Highway 20. Several Forest Service campgrounds and two private campgrounds also exist on or near this Highway 20 section, per the website.

wow_evidence: the only provincial campsite along Highway 20 between Williams Lake and Tweedsmuir Park
